title: Pepper Steak with Onions
seoTitle: Pepper Steak with Onions | Firefighter Meal
shortDescription: Sliced round steak with bell peppers over rice for ten
subtitle: Sliced round steak with bell peppers over rice for ten
description: Round steak strips marinate in soy and ginger, stir-fry with peppers and onions, and finish in a savory gravy. Serve over steamed rice for a filling hall plate.

steps.title: Gather ingredients and equipment
steps.instruction: Line up every ingredient for Pepper Steak with Onions in the order you will cook — measure spices into ramekins, trim proteins on a dedicated board, and set tongs, thermometers, and hotel pans within arm's reach before any heat goes on.

steps.title: Preheat ovens and surfaces
steps.instruction: Preheat ovens, griddles, or grills to recipe temp before the crew arrives — cold equipment extends cook time and dries out batch beef. Confirm burners ignite evenly and sheet pans are greased or lined.

steps.title: Marinate and prep rice
steps.instruction: Toss sliced steak with half the soy sauce and ginger. Start rice in a pot with 6 cups water—bring to boil, cover, simmer 18 minutes, then rest off heat. Target 145°F for steaks, 160°F for ground at the thickest point before moving to the next batch.

steps.title: Sear the beef
steps.instruction: Heat oil in a wok over high heat. Stir-fry beef in batches 2–3 minutes until browned but still tender. Set aside. Cook until char marks are visible and the thickest piece reads 145°F for medium beef, 160°F for ground on an instant-read thermometer. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

steps.title: Stir-fry vegetables
steps.instruction: Add peppers and onion to the wok. Stir-fry 4–5 minutes until charred at edges and slightly softened. Target 145°F for medium beef, 160°F for ground at the thickest part before moving to the next batch. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

steps.title: Build the gravy
steps.instruction: Stir remaining soy sauce, garlic, broth, and cornstarch slurry into the wok. Simmer 2 minutes until glossy and thickened. Maintain a steady simmer — bubbles should break the surface without a rolling boil that shreds delicate proteins. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

steps.title: Verify safe internal temps
steps.instruction: Spot-check the thickest pieces with an instant-read thermometer — target 145°F for medium beef, 160°F for ground. If any piece reads low, return it to heat immediately rather than holding under temp on the line.

steps.title: Hold for call interruptions
steps.instruction: If tones drop mid-service, cover finished food and hold at 140°F in a warm cabinet or 200°F oven — never leave proteins below 140°F for more than 30 minutes cumulative. Note the hold time on the pan with a grease pencil.

steps.title: Combine and serve
steps.instruction: Return beef and juices to gravy, toss 1 minute to coat. Fluff rice and serve pepper steak over rice at the line. Keep finished cold items below 41°F if they sit more than 30 minutes — nest the hotel pan on ice at the line. Keep a backup tray at 200°F for firefighters returning from a call — never serve picked-over pans to late crew.

proTips: A splash of rice vinegar at the end brightens heavy soy gravy.
Use baking soda pinch in marinade for extra tender beef if your cut is tough.
Sesame oil drizzle at service adds aroma—do not cook it on high heat.
tonightSpread: Pepper steak over rice with steamed broccoli on the side.
Chili garlic crisp at the table for crew who want more heat.
leftovers: Wrap in flour tortillas with extra sauce for quick lunch wraps.
Stir into fried rice the next day with scrambled eggs.
whyCrewsLikeIt: Pepper steak delivers big savory flavor with ingredients already in the station pantry. Rice stretches the protein and keeps everyone full through a second call.
mealPrepNotes: Slice steak against the grain paper-thin. Mix gravy slurry before you start cooking—no time to measure mid-stir-fry. Cook rice in a separate pot or rice cooker.
